items.title: Mississauga Planning Staff Recommend Keeping Existing 20-Storey Tower in New Dixie-Rathburn Rental Proposal
items.summary: According to a report to Mississauga's Planning and Development Committee, planning staff are recommending approval of a 144 unit infill rental building near Dixie and Rathburn roads, on a site that already holds a 20-storey tower. The committee is set to vote on the proposal Nov. 23, the report says. The plan replaces an earlier proposal for two 18-storey buildings linked by a podium, and would keep the existing tower and some surface parking while adding an underground garage with 159 spots. Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca met earlier this year with residents of the existing building, per the report. Residents raised concerns about traffic, parking, pedestrian safety, construction noise and loss of natural light, the report states. Traffic studies found only acceptable delay increases, and the city will secure a daylight triangle at Bough Beeches and Rathburn Road East for visibility.

items.title: Non-Residents Must Wait Until December for Mississauga's Winter and March Break Program Sign-Ups
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, winter recreational programs and March break camps are now posted online ahead of registration, which opens for local residents on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The city says non-residents can begin signing up starting Dec. 1. Residents can register either through the Active Mississauga website or in person at a community centre during service desk hours, according to the city. Officials are encouraging residents to browse and bookmark their preferred programs beforehand, noting that popular offerings fill up quickly. The city says the programs are open to people of all ages and abilities across a range of activities. Mississauga directs residents seeking more details to its news release or website for further registration information.

items.title: White SUV Strikes and Kills Pedestrian on Erindale Station Road, Closing Lanes Through Dundas Street
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a male pedestrian was struck and killed by a vehicle in the area of Erindale Station Road and Dundas Street in Mississauga on Thursday evening. Police say the man was pronounced dead after being hit, and no further details about the victim have been released. Officers told reporters that a white SUV was travelling south on Erindale Station Road when it struck him. Police say the driver of the vehicle remained at the scene following the collision. All lanes have been closed on Erindale Station Road between Forestwood Drive and Dundas Street West while officers investigate, according to police. Police are asking drivers to avoid the area and find alternate routes while the road remains closed.

items.title: Fourth Automated Pumping Station Set to Begin Construction as Mississauga Targets Flood-Prone Northwest
items.summary: According to Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden, construction is set to begin next week on a fourth automated pumping station meant to protect a northwest Mississauga community that has faced severe flooding for years. McFadden told constituents the city has awarded the contract for the long awaited facility, following a third station running in the Lisgar area of west Meadowvale since August. City officials say the new infrastructure at Osprey Marsh is critical to shielding homes in the city's northwest corner from major flooding. The councillor said the station pumps water out of the Foundation Drain Collector system, adding capacity to prevent backups during storms or sudden snow melt. McFadden said the station will sit at the east end of Osprey Marsh, near Osprey Boulevard, and should be operational by December 2027. She added a construction notice has gone to nearby properties.

items.title: Milton Massage Business Sees Second Sexual Assault Charge Against Same Mississauga Therapist
items.summary: According to Halton Regional Police, a Mississauga man who worked as a registered massage therapist in Milton has been charged with sexual assault after a woman came forward to police. Police say the charge stems from an alleged assault in May 2025, when the suspect was employed at Massage Addict on Steeles Avenue in Milton. Investigators with the force's Child Abuse and Sexual Assault Unit said they began looking into the complaint last month. Police identified the accused as Ayman Alkassem, 53, of Mississauga, arrested Nov. 19 and charged with one count of sexual assault, according to a news release. Alkassem has been held in custody pending a bail hearing in Milton court. Police noted Alkassem was also charged with sexual assault in June 2025 over another alleged incident at the same business, and said he had worked at other studios too, including more locations in Mississauga.

items.title: Peel Police Keep Hunting 2022 Gas Station Murder Suspect After He Drops Off National Wanted List
items.summary: According to the BOLO Program, a man wanted in the 2022 killing of a young woman at a Mississauga gas station is still being actively pursued despite falling off Canada's top 25 most wanted fugitives list. The program's updated list, revealed Thursday, no longer includes Dharam Dhaliwal, 33, who had appeared on its 2024 to 2025 and 2025 to 2026 rosters. BOLO, whose name comes from the police term be on the lookout, says it uses social media to raise awareness of wanted suspects, working with police and Crime Stoppers programs nationwide. Dhaliwal is wanted by Peel Regional Police on a first degree murder warrant and first appeared among Canada's 25 most wanted in April 2024, when he ranked ninth. He later moved to 15th, and in BOLO's late 2025 update he sat at 21st before dropping off the newest list. Police say Dhaliwal remains sought in the December 2022 gas station murder.
